assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single molecules through the ionic current blocked in a nanopore rests on a clean physical principle and has become a general-purpose single-molecule sensing platform. It delivered long-read DNA/RNA sequencing, direct detection of modified bases and portable instruments, so it opens genuinely new capability. The chemistry lies in engineered protein pores and the molecular motors that ratchet strands through them, which is close to my own field of thermal ratchets.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton conceived and pursued strand translocation through pores; Bayley engineered alpha-hemolysin and later pores and enzyme-assisted schemes that made base discrimination real. Kasianowicz and Akeson made early or key experimental demonstrations, so a three-person citation is defensible but leaves out important contributors and the commercial engineering is separate from the discovery.
assessment.maturity: Over a decade of independent validation and widespread routine use in genomics and field sequencing. Recognition looks timely, and the interpretation of the principle is stable even though accuracy continues to improve.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as physics/biotechnology, and the Medicine and Physics overlap.
Relative weight of Kasianowicz and Akeson against Deamer, Branton and Bayley is judged from memory, not verified here.
Deamer's and Branton's roles in the original idea versus later demonstrations may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one nucleotide to another without double-strand breaks by engineering deaminases fused to a programmable DNA-binding protein. It is a clear, original chemical-biology invention with a quantitative, mechanistic basis, and it opened a new class of precise genome edits and therapies (already in clinical trials).
assessment.attribution: Liu directed the work; Komor made the first cytosine base editors and Gaudelli the adenine base editors, which required directed evolution of a deaminase acting on DNA. The Japanese deaminase-CRISPR work (Nishida, Kondo) was concurrent and is a credit question. A prize naming Liu, Komor and Gaudelli is workable though Liu is the obvious anchor and prime editing (a separate candidate) could be folded in.
assessment.maturity: Therapeutic proof of concept is accumulating, but long-term clinical outcomes are still limited. The 2020 CRISPR prize makes this a follow-on, and the committee must be sure of the distinct invention.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with the separate prime-editing candidate.
Whether junior contributors Komor and Gaudelli should be included at the expense of the concurrent Nishida/Kondo work.
Clinical durability is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cells from a few percent to above 25 percent efficiency in a little over a decade, a remarkable rise driven by defect tolerance and long carrier diffusion lengths. It is a materials-chemistry result with strong generative potential, but the physical explanation for the performance is still being worked out.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell (with Kojima, who is not on this credited list), Park achieved the solid-state stable device, and Snaith showed the meso-superstructured and planar architectures. Grätzel and Seok, Kanatzidis are also strong claims. The attribution is crowded and a fair three-person selection is hard.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is independently confirmed, but long-term operational stability and lead toxicity remain unresolved and commercial deployment is early, so the prize could be premature.
uncertainties: Stability and deployment are unproven.
Kojima is missing from the credited names although part of the first report.
Competing claims among Grätzel, Seok, Kanatzidis, Snaith and Park make the selection arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Orbitrap uses an electrostatic trap with image-current detection and Fourier transformation to give very high resolution and mass accuracy. It is a physically elegant invention that reshaped proteomics, metabolomics and small-molecule analysis, and I find a measurement at near a fundamental limit particularly compelling.
assessment.attribution: Makarov is the clear inventor, building on Kingdon-trap ideas; the single-person credit is unambiguous, though a prize usually requires a pair or trio and a co-laureate from the application side would have to come from outside this candidate's names.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for more than twenty years and independently validated, so mature and timely.
uncertainties: A sole inventor of an instrument is unusual for a chemistry prize and the committee might favour a combined mass-spectrometry citation.
Dependence on earlier Kingdon trap physics could be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to the ubiquitin ligase machinery to degrade proteins previously considered undruggable is a new pharmacological principle. PROTACs and molecular glues, including the mechanism of thalidomide analogues through cereblon, have produced many clinical candidates.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Ciulli, Gray and others contributed important later work, so the group is large and a trio will leave out real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is accumulating but no PROTAC drug is yet widely approved, so the maturity is arguably early.
uncertainties: Lack of approved PROTAC therapeutics.
Whether molecular glues and PROTACs should be recognised together.
Crowded attribution including Ito, Sakamoto, Kim, Ciulli and Gray.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N coupling is a general method that is used daily in pharmaceutical synthesis, built on mechanistic understanding of ligand design. The importance is high but it is an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general, ligand-controlled methods, and Kosugi's earlier tin amide work is a precursor. A two-person citation is natural.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and decades old, so recognition is long overdue if the committee accepts it as distinct from 2010.
uncertainties: Whether the 2010 prize already covers the principle and weakens the case.
Credit to Kosugi and Migita as precursors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as a mechanism for organising cellular compartments introduces a physical-chemistry principle that is familiar to a physicist and reshapes cell biology. It has produced a wide field of research and quantitative frameworks.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman reported P granule liquid behaviour, and Rosen showed multivalent phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical theory and sequence grammar, which is a difficult allocation.
assessment.maturity: The field is still contested; the physiological relevance and the interpretation of condensates are debated and much evidence depends on overexpression, so it may be premature.
uncertainties: Physiological relevance is controversial.
Whether the discovery is chemistry rather than biology.
Fair allocation among five major contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis uses excited-state electron transfer to enable new bond constructions under mild conditions and is broadly used in synthesis. The principle is clear and generative.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson independently revived the field in 2008, but MacMillan is already a laureate (2021), and König, Fukuzumi, Nicewicz and Melchiorre are also credited, so a trio is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and confirmed, but the committee may consider the 2021 organocatalysis prize as having already recognised part of it.
uncertainties: Prior laureate status of MacMillan.
Priority claims from earlier photochemistry such as Fukuzumi and Kellogg or Cano-Yelo and Deronzier.
Credit allocation among seven names.
